assignedReviews.card_evidence: Looking closely is part of doing the experiment! Watch the color, bubbles, or wetness, then write those clues right beside the time.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the steps of a simple science investigation (What is the problem? What materials do you need? What do you need to do? What have you found out/learned?)
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a tip about observing and recording clues during an experiment, which is a useful background skill for carrying out an investigation, but it does not describe the steps of a simple science investigation (problem, materials, procedure, findings) as required by the competency.

copy.en: Looking closely is part of doing the experiment! Watch the color, bubbles, or wetness, then write those clues right beside the time.
copy.tl: Ang pagmasid nang mabuti ay parte ng paggawa! Panoorin ang color, bubbles, o wetness, tapos isulat ang mga clues kasama ang time.
copy.bis: Ang pagtan-aw og tarong parte sa pagbuhat! Tan-awa ang color, bubbles, o wetness, dayon isulat ang mga clues kauban ang time.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Dolphins talk using whistles and clicking sounds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions sounds (whistles and clicks) but does not describe how sound is made or transferred, which is the core of G3-F-4. It is about animal communication, not sound production/transfer.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: each one even has its own 'signature whistle' that works just like a name
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes dolphin communication, not the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It does not directly support G3-L-3.

copy.en: Dolphins talk using whistles and clicking sounds — each one even has its own 'signature whistle' that works just like a name.
copy.tl: Nakikipag-usap ang mga dolphin gamit ang mga sutsot at kalantog na tunog — may sariling 'signature whistle' ang bawat isa na parang pangalan nito.
copy.bis: Makigsulti ang mga dolphin gamit ang mga sutsot ug kalantog nga tingog — matag usa adunay kaugalingong 'signature whistle' nga morag ngalan niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They send out fast clicking sounds and listen to the echoes to find fish and other objects!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes sound being produced and an echo being received, but it is about dolphin echolocation, not the everyday sound situations (bell ringing, hearing noises) that the competency targets. It shares the sound vocabulary but does not directly teach the grade 3 skill of exploring and describing how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They send out fast clicking sounds and listen to the echoes to find fish and other objects!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that waves carry energy from a source to a receiver
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions sound traveling from a source (dolphin) to a receiver (dolphin via echo), but it does not identify or explain that waves carry energy. It is an example of sound use, not instruction on the wave-energy concept required by the competency.

copy.en:
How do dolphins find food in the water?

They send out fast clicking sounds and listen to the echoes to find fish and other objects!
copy.tl:
Paano naghahanap ng pagkain ang lumba-lumba sa tubig?

Nagpapadala sila ng mabibilis na tunog na kumakalantog at nakikinig sa alingawngaw para mahanap ang isda!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagpangita og pagkaon sa lumba-lumba sa tubig?

Mopadala sila og paspas nga nagaklik nga tingog ug mamati sa alingawngaw aron makapangita og isda!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: no light from the raindrops reaches your eyes from that exact spot
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a specific optical phenomenon (Alexander's band) but does not address sources of light, how light behaves or can be changed in the general sense, or uses in everyday situations. It is not tied to a guided activity and is too advanced for Grade 3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: no light from the raindrops reaches your eyes from that exact spot
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions light behavior in rainbows but does not describe or illustrate reflection using mirrors or refraction using transparent blocks, lenses, or prisms, nor does it include guided investigations or everyday applications. It is only tangentially related to the properties of light.

copy.en: See that dark strip between the two rainbows? It's called Alexander's band! It looks dark because no light from the raindrops reaches your eyes from that exact spot.
copy.tl: May madilim na guhit sa pagitan ng dalawang bahaghari — Alexander's band! Madilim ito dahil walang liwanag mula sa patak ng ulan ang umaabot sa mata mo sa lugar na iyon.
copy.bis: Naay mas ngitngit nga hawid taliwala sa duha ka bahaghari — Alexander's band! Ngitngit kini kay walay kahayag gikan sa tinulo sa ulan nga moabot sa imong mata niana nga dapit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The second rainbow always appears OUTSIDE and higher than the first one.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the position and appearance of a secondary rainbow but does not mention light, its sources, behavior, or uses. It does not directly support the competency's focus on exploring and describing light behavior. It is only related to light phenomena through the general topic of rainbows.

copy.en: The second rainbow always appears OUTSIDE and higher than the first one. Its arc is wider, so it looks like it sits above and around the main bow!
copy.tl: Ang pangalawang bahaghari ay laging nasa LABAS at mas mataas kaysa sa una. Mas malaki ang arko nito, kaya parang nakapatong sa ibabaw at paligid ng unang bahaghari!
copy.bis: Ang ikaduhang bahaghari kanunay anaa sa GAWAS ug mas taas kaysa nauna. Mas dako ang arko niini, mao nga morag nagpatong sa ibabaw ug palibot sa nauna!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An insulated cup keeps the outside cool!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an insulated cup as keeping the outside cool, which is an everyday example of reducing heat transfer. However, it does not identify or explain conduction, convection, or radiation, nor does it present advantageous/disadvantageous examples of these specific mechanisms. The content is only tangentially related to heat transfer concepts.

copy.en:
How can you hold a cup with a hot drink inside?

An insulated cup keeps the outside cool! The drink inside stays hot, but the outside is safe to hold.
copy.tl:
Paano mo mahahawakan ang baso na may mainit na inumin sa loob?

Ang insulated na baso ay nagpapabugnaw sa labas! Mainit ang loob, pero ligtas mong hawakan ang panlabas.
copy.bis:
Unsaon nimo pagkupot sa baso nga naay init nga ilimnon sa sulod?

Ang insulated nga baso nagpabilin nga bugnaw ang gawas! Init ang sulod, apan luwas nimo kuptan ang gawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A dragonfly has huge eyes that cover most of its head, letting it see in almost every direction at once!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an outer body part (eyes) and its role in vision, but the competency specifically requires identifying roles to move and to gather food. Vision is not movement or food gathering, so the card does not directly support the stated skill.

copy.en:
Why can dragonflies see almost everywhere?

A dragonfly has huge eyes that cover most of its head, letting it see in almost every direction at once!
copy.tl:
Bakit nakakakita ang tutubi sa halos lahat ng direksyon?

May napakalaking mata ang tutubi na halos bumabalot sa buong ulo nito, kaya nakakakita ito sa halos lahat ng direksyon!
copy.bis:
Nganong makakita ang tutubi sa halos tanang direksyon?

Adunay dagkong kaayo nga mata ang tutubi nga halos motabon sa tibuok ulo niini, mao nga makakita kini sa halos tanang direksyon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The draisine had no pedals, so the rider pushed it along the ground with their feet!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the draisine, an early bicycle, and how it was ridden, but it does not identify any scientist (Filipino or foreign) or attribute the invention to a specific person. The competency requires using secondary sources to identify a scientist and their invention; the card only mentions an invention without a scientist, so it is related to the topic of inventions but does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
How did people ride the first bicycle if it had no pedals?

The draisine had no pedals, so the rider pushed it along the ground with their feet!
copy.tl:
Paano sumakay sa unang bisikleta kung wala itong pedal?

Walang pedal ang draisine, kaya itinutulak ito ng mananakay gamit ang kanilang mga paa sa lupa!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagsakay sa unang bisikleta kung wala man kiniy pedal?

Walay pedal ang draisine, mao nga gitulod kini sa nagsakay gamit ang ilang mga tiil sa yuta!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: During diarrhea and vomiting, it's important to drink plenty of fluids to avoid dehydration.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions diarrhea and vomiting, which involve the digestive system, but it does not describe how any body system works. It is a health tip about fluid intake, not an explanation of digestive, muscular, skeletal, circulatory, or respiratory function.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: During diarrhea and vomiting, it's important to drink plenty of fluids to avoid dehydration.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: Dehydration relates to fluid balance, a component of homeostasis, but the card does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems, nor does it mention indicators such as body temperature, glucose level, or blood pressure. It only gives a practical recommendation without explaining the concept.

copy.en: During diarrhea and vomiting, it's important to drink plenty of fluids to avoid dehydration.
copy.tl: Kapag may pagtatae at pagsusuka, mahalagang uminom ng maraming tubig para hindi ma-dehydrate.
copy.bis: Kung naay kalibanga ug pagsuka, importante moinom og daghang tubig aron dili mamala ang lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When mineral-rich water drips, it leaves thin rock layers that slowly build stalactites and stalagmites!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes deposition of minerals from dripping water to build stalactites/stalagmites, not erosion transporting Earth materials. It shares the topic of Earth materials but does not support the erosion competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When mineral-rich water drips, it leaves thin rock layers that slowly build stalactites and stalagmites!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions rock layers but does not involve observing or collecting different types of rocks or comparing features like texture, color, or grain crystal size. It is about a specific cave formation process, not rock classification.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When mineral-rich water drips, it leaves thin rock layers that slowly build stalactites and stalagmites!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not identify local landforms or bodies of water, nor describe their influence on living and non-living components. Stalactites/stalagmites are not among the listed landforms (mountains, valleys, rivers, coastlines).

copy.en:
How do stalactites and stalagmites form?

When mineral-rich water drips, it leaves thin rock layers that slowly build stalactites and stalagmites!
copy.tl:
Paano nabubuo ang stalactite at stalagmite?

Kapag tumutulo ang tubig na may mineral, naiiwan ang manipis na bato na unti-unting bumubuo ng stalactite at stalagmite!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagporma sa stalactite ug stalagmite?

Kung motulo ang tubig nga puno og mineral, mabilin ang nipis nga bato nga hinay-hinayng mohimo sa stalactite ug stalagmite!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Air and heat sneak into the gaps, pulling water from inside!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of the water cycle in the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes evaporation of water from soil, which is a component of the water cycle, but it does not explain the role of the water cycle in the environment. It only touches on one process without connecting it to the broader cycle.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Air and heat sneak into the gaps, pulling water from inside!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies water changing from liquid to gas due to heat, but it does not explicitly describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change state. It focuses on soil cracking, not on the state change itself.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Air and heat sneak into the gaps, pulling water from inside!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions evaporation indirectly but does not describe changes of state (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) using diagrams or flowcharts. It lacks the required format and does not teach the competency directly.

copy.en:
Why do cracks make soil dry faster?

Air and heat sneak into the gaps, pulling water from inside! This tricky cycle turns small cracks into bigger ones.
copy.tl:
Bakit mas mabilis matuyo ang lupa kapag may bitak?

Pumapasok ang hangin at init sa mga puwang, inaalis ang tubig! Kaya lumalaki ang mga bitak.
copy.bis:
Nganong mas paspas mamala ang yuta kon naa nay liki?

Mosulod ang hangin ug init sa mga lungag, mokuha sa tubig! Mao nga modako ang mga liki.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Dry ground cracks often form neat, blocky shapes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities using simple equipment to compare different types of soil including sandy, clay, silt, and loam, including comparing the ability of the soils to hold water
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses soil cracking due to even inward pulling, but does not compare different soil types (sandy, clay, silt, loam) or their water-holding ability. It only mentions soil in a general way, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Dry ground cracks often form neat, blocky shapes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about observing and collecting rocks and describing their texture, color, and grain crystal size. The card is about cracks in dry soil, not rocks, and provides no information about rock features. It is unrelated to the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Dry ground cracks often form neat, blocky shapes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The competency asks to describe physical properties of solid materials such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. The card describes a pattern formed by drying soil, not a physical property of a solid material. It does not teach hardness, shininess, or stretchability, so it is only tangentially related.

copy.en: Dry ground cracks often form neat, blocky shapes like tiny six-sided or four-sided puzzle pieces! This happens because the soil pulls inward evenly on all sides.
copy.tl: Ang mga bitak sa tuyong lupa ay madalas na hugis maliliit na anim o apat na sulok na nagdidikit! Nangyayari ito dahil ang lupa ay humihila pababa nang pantay sa lahat ng panig.
copy.bis: Ang mga liki sa mala nga yuta kasagaran og porma nga gagmay nga unom o upat ka kilid nga magtapad! Mahitabo kini kay ang yuta mobira paingon sa sulod nga patas sa tanang kilid.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: water might remain trapped in their lungs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions lungs but does not identify respiratory system parts (nose, windpipe, lungs) or describe how they work. It is a health-safety tip about post-drowning medical care, not instruction on the respiratory system.

copy.en: Even after someone is rescued from nearly drowning, they still need a doctor's check-up, because water might remain trapped in their lungs.
copy.tl: Kahit nailigtas na ang isang taong halos malunod, kailangan pa rin siyang dalhin sa doktor dahil maaaring may natitirang tubig sa kanyang baga.
copy.bis: Bisan naluwas na ang tawo nga halos malumos, kinahanglan gihapon siyang dad-on sa doktor kay basin adunay nahabilin nga tubig sa iyang baga.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Dry ice is carbon dioxide in solid form, and it turns directly into gas in the air!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions solid and gas but does not identify the three states of matter (solid, liquid, gas) or teach the concept of three states.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Dry ice is carbon dioxide in solid form, and it turns directly into gas in the air!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe shape or volume properties of solids, liquids, or gases; it only names two states.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it turns directly into gas in the air!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a solid-to-gas change but does not describe the named processes (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) or use diagrams/flowcharts as required.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it turns directly into gas in the air!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card shows a solid-to-gas change but does not explain how temperature causes state changes or address the solid-to-liquid-to-gas sequence.

copy.en:
What is dry ice made of?

Dry ice is carbon dioxide in solid form, and it turns directly into gas in the air!
copy.tl:
Ano ang dry ice?

Ang dry ice ay carbon dioxide na nasa solid na anyo, at direktang nagiging gas sa hangin!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang dry ice?

Ang dry ice mao ang carbon dioxide sa solid nga porma, ug diretsong mahimong gas sa hangin!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It turns straight into a gas without becoming a liquid first
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes sublimation (solid to gas), but G6-M-1 specifically requires describing melting, evaporation, freezing, and condensation using diagrams and flowcharts. Sublimation is not among the listed processes, and the card contains no diagram or flowchart.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It turns straight into a gas without becoming a liquid first
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: G5-M-6 focuses on temperature-driven changes of state such as solid to liquid to gas. The card describes a solid-to-gas change (sublimation) without mentioning temperature as the cause, and it does not address the solid-to-liquid-to-gas sequence. It is only tangentially related to changes of state.

copy.en:
Why does dry ice make thick, cloud-like smoke?

Dry ice is solid carbon dioxide! It turns straight into a gas without becoming a liquid first, creating that cool smoke.
copy.tl:
Bakit gumagawa ng makapal na usok na parang ulap ang dry ice?

Ang dry ice ay matigas na carbon dioxide! Direktang nagiging gas ito nang hindi nauuna sa likido kaya gumagawa ng makapal na usok.
copy.bis:
Nganong makahimo ug baga nga aso nga daw panganod ang dry ice?

Ang dry ice gahi nga carbon dioxide! Diretsong mahimong gas kini nga dili una mahimong likido mao nga makahimo ug baga nga aso.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They are related birds that belong to the same group of swimming waterfowl
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that ducks and geese are related birds in the same group of swimming waterfowl, but it does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups (mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians, etc.) as required by the competency. It only mentions a general grouping of birds without the required table or classification into the specified categories.

copy.en:
Are ducks and geese related?

Yes! They are related birds that belong to the same group of swimming waterfowl.
copy.tl:
Magkamag-anak ba ang bibe at gansa?

Oo! Magkamag-anak silang mga ibon dahil pareho silang nabibilang sa pangkat ng mga ibong palangoy.
copy.bis:
Managsoon ba ang bibe ug gansa?

Oo! Managsoon sila nga mga langgam kay parehong sakop sa grupo sa mga langgam nga maglangoy.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: drinks her milk
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a dugong calf nursing, which is a mammalian trait, but it does not identify groups that give birth to live young versus those that lay eggs. It does not mention live birth or egg-laying, so it does not directly support the competency's classification action.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A baby dugong stays close to its mother and drinks her milk until it's fully grown.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a dugong from birth to adulthood, but it does not compare life cycles of mammals, birds, and plants. It only gives a single fact about a dugong calf nursing, not a comparison of stages across groups.

copy.en: A baby dugong stays close to its mother and drinks her milk until it's fully grown.
copy.tl: Ang batang dugong ay palaging malapit sa kanyang ina at sumususo ng gatas nito hanggang lumaki.
copy.bis: Ang nati nga dugong kanunay duol sa iyang inahan ug mosuso og gatas niini hangtod modako.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the dugong is often called 'duyong'
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a list or draw up a table with examples of animals and plants in a particular habitat, such as a garden, rice field, seashore, and mangrove swamp
assignedReviews.reason: The card only gives the local Filipino name for a single sea animal. It does not make a list or table of animals and plants in a particular habitat, nor does it provide examples of multiple organisms in a named habitat. The format-required list/table is absent, so the card does not directly support G4-L-4.

copy.en: In the Philippines, the dugong is often called 'duyong' — so 'duyong' and 'dugong' both mean the exact same sea animal.
copy.tl: Sa Pilipinas, ang dugong ay madalas tawaging 'duyong.' Kaya kung marinig mong 'duyong,' iisang hayop lang din ito sa dagat.
copy.bis: Sa Pilipinas, ang dugong kasagarang gitawag 'duyong.' Mao nga ang 'duyong' ug 'dugong' usa ra ka hayop sa dagat.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The dugong moves slowly because the seagrass it eats gives little energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that dugongs eat seagrass, which is plant material, but it does not group animals into herbivores, carnivores, or omnivores, nor does it use secondary sources to classify animals by diet. The diet fact is incidental to the energy explanation, not instructional support for the grouping competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: so it saves strength by staying gentle and unhurried
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a behavioral adaptation (slow movement) linked to a low-energy diet, but it does not describe how animals have changed to better suit their environment through mimicry, camouflage, or other evolutionary changes. The slow movement is a current behavior, not an example of adaptation over time, and the card does not support the competency's focus on animals changing to suit their environment.

copy.en: The dugong moves slowly because the seagrass it eats gives little energy, so it saves strength by staying gentle and unhurried.
copy.tl: Mabagal kumilos ang dugong dahil kakaunti ang enerhiyang ibinibigay ng damong-dagat na kinakain nito, kaya nagtitipid ito ng lakas sa dahan-dahang paggalaw.
copy.bis: Hinay molihok ang dugong kay gamay ra og enerhiya ang gihatag sa sagbot sa dagat nga iyang gikaon, mao nga nagtipig kini og kusog pinaagi sa hinay nga paglihok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: There are three kinds of dung beetle: rollers roll dung away, tunnelers dig beneath it, and dwellers just live inside it
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: rollers roll dung away, tunnelers dig beneath it, and dwellers just live inside it
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: Rolling or tunneling dung is not head, legs or wings used to move and gather food.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: There are three kinds of dung beetle: rollers roll dung away, tunnelers dig beneath it, and dwellers just live inside it
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web
assignedReviews.reason: Three dung-beetle habits is not the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web.

copy.en: There are three kinds of dung beetle: rollers roll dung away, tunnelers dig beneath it, and dwellers just live inside it!
copy.tl: May tatlong uri ng dung beetle: ang rollers ay iginugulong ang dumi, ang tunnelers ay naghuhukay sa ilalim nito, at ang dwellers ay naninirahan sa loob nito!
copy.bis: Adunay tulo ka matang sa dung beetle: ang rollers moligid sa tae, ang tunnelers mokalot ubos niini, ug ang dwellers nagpuyo lang sulod niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The part of durian people actually eat is the soft, tasty flesh hidden inside its spiky skin.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the edible flesh inside a durian fruit, which is not an outer plant part (leaves, roots, stems) and does not address the role of such parts in obtaining water and nutrients from the soil. It shares only the broad topic of plant parts.

copy.en: The part of durian people actually eat is the soft, tasty flesh hidden inside its spiky skin.
copy.tl: Ang kinakain sa durian ay ang malambot at malinamnam na laman sa loob ng matinik na balat nito.
copy.bis: Ang ginakaon sa durian mao ang humok ug lami nga unod sa sulod sa tunokon nga panit niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Inside a durian are several sections, like little rooms — each holding soft flesh with seeds.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the internal structure of a durian fruit, not the outer parts of plants (leaves, roots, stems) or their role in water and nutrient uptake. No direct or prerequisite support for G3-L-5.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Inside a durian are several sections, like little rooms — each holding soft flesh with seeds.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the purpose of specialized structures in plants, such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, and aerial roots
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a plant structure (fruit sections) but does not describe the purpose of specialized structures such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, or aerial roots. It shares the broad topic of plant structures but provides no instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: Inside a durian are several sections, like little rooms — each holding soft flesh with seeds. Opening it splits the fruit into these sections.
copy.tl: May ilang bahagi o silid sa loob ng durian, parang maliliit na kuwarto — bawat isa ay may malambot na lamang may buto. Kapag binuksan, naghahati ito sa mga bahaging ito.
copy.bis: Adunay pipila ka bahin o silid sa sulod sa durian, morag gagmayng kwarto — matag usa adunay humok nga unod nga adunay liso. Kon ablihan, mabahin kini sa mga bahin.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Durian is packed with natural sugar, giving you energy and nutrients in every bite!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a food item (durian) and its energy/nutrient content, but does not identify or teach the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter). It only tangentially relates to food as a need.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Durian is packed with natural sugar, giving you energy and nutrients in every bite!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a fruit's nutritional content, not the functioning of any human body system (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory). It provides no instructional support for this competency.

copy.en: Durian is packed with natural sugar, giving you energy and nutrients in every bite!
copy.tl: Ang durian ay mayaman sa natural na asukal, kaya nagbibigay ito ng lakas at sustansya!
copy.bis: Ang durian dato sa natural nga asukal, mao nga naghatag kini og kusog ug sustansya!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: helps natural dyes bond permanently to fabric
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that the formation of new bonds or the breaking of existing bonds constitutes a chemical change and the formation of a new substance
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions bonding but does not explain that bond formation/breaking constitutes a chemical change or the formation of a new substance. It is a brief example of a chemical process, not instruction on the competency's core concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A mordant like tawas is a chemical that helps natural dyes bond permanently to fabric
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a chemical's function but does not describe chemical properties such as being burnt, reacting with other materials, or being degradable/biodegradable. It only touches on a chemical reaction in a general way.

copy.en: A mordant like tawas is a chemical that helps natural dyes bond permanently to fabric, so the color won't quickly wash out!
copy.tl: Ang mordant tulad ng tawas ay kemikal na tumutulong sa natural na dye na permanenteng kumapit sa tela, kaya hindi mabilis mawala ang kulay!
copy.bis: Ang mordant sama sa tawas usa ka kemikal nga nagtabang sa natural nga dye nga permanenteng modikit sa tela, aron dili dali mapupo ang kolor!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Its shape and length create natural resonance that amplifies sounds between 2,000 and 5,000 Hz
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses hearing and resonance in the ear canal, but does not explore or describe how sound is made or transferred in everyday situations. It is only tangentially related to sound and hearing.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: amplifies sounds between 2,000 and 5,000 Hz
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: research using secondary sources to identify how the properties of waves are described using scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions frequency (Hz) but does not describe wave properties using scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and velocity. It does not support the research/description skill of the competency.

copy.en:
How does your ear canal help you understand speech?

Its shape and length create natural resonance that amplifies sounds between 2,000 and 5,000 Hz, which is the exact range for understanding speech!
copy.tl:
Paano nakakatulong ang ear canal mo para maintindihan ang salita?

Ang hugis at haba nito ay gumagawa ng natural resonance na nagpapalaki ng tunog sa pagitan ng 2,000 at 5,000 Hz, ang eksaktong hanay para sa pag-unawa ng salita!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagtabang sa imong ear canal aron masabtan ang sinultian?

Ang porma ug gitas-on niini nagahatag og natural nga resonance nga nagapalaka sa mga tunog tali sa 2,000 ug 5,000 Hz, ang hanay nga pinaka-importante sa pagsabot sa sinultian!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: During the Industrial Revolution, many factory machines were powered by steam engines fueled by coal!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a science invention (steam engine) but does not involve using information from the home or local community, nor does it explain the invention's impact on everyday life. It is a general historical fact, so it only shares the broad subject of science inventions.

copy.en: During the Industrial Revolution, many factory machines were powered by steam engines fueled by coal!
copy.tl: Sa Rebolusyong Industriyal, maraming makina sa pabrika ang pinapaandar ng steam engine na gatong ang coal!
copy.bis: Atol sa Industrial Revolution, daghang makina sa pabrika ang gipaandar sa steam engine nga ang gatong mao ang coal!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your ears are the body parts you use to hear all the sounds around you!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that ears are used to hear sounds. It does not explore or describe how sound is made or transferred, which is the core of the competency. The mention of hearing is a superficial link, not direct instructional support.

copy.en: Your ears are the body parts you use to hear all the sounds around you!
copy.tl: Ang tainga ang bahagi ng katawan na ginagamit natin para makarinig ng tunog!
copy.bis: Ang dalunggan mao ang bahin sa lawas nga atong gigamit aron makadungog og tingog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It is about 4.5 billion years old.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how the geologic time scale helps to recount the history of the Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states Earth's age. It does not explain the geologic time scale or how it helps recount Earth's history, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It is about 4.5 billion years old.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how relative and absolute dating techniques are used to determine the subdivisions of geologic time
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an age but does not describe relative or absolute dating techniques or how they determine subdivisions of geologic time. It is only tangentially related.

copy.en: Planet Earth is very, very old! It is about 4.5 billion years old.
copy.tl: Ang Mundo ay napakatanda na! May edad na itong halos 4.5 bilyong taon.
copy.bis: Ang planeta Kalibutan kay karaan kaayo! Mga 4.5 ka bilyon ka tuig na ang edad.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The distance around the Earth (its circumference) at the equator is about 40,000 kilometers!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a single measurement of Earth's circumference. G5-E-11 requires describing the general structure of the solar system, naming major celestial objects, and describing their main features and composition. A single size fact about Earth does not directly support describing the solar system's structure or the features/composition of celestial objects.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The distance around the Earth (its circumference) at the equator is about 40,000 kilometers!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: G3-E-6 is about observing and describing natural objects seen in the sky (Sun, Moon, planets, stars). Earth is not an object seen in the sky from Earth, and the card provides no observational or descriptive content about sky objects. The fact about Earth's circumference is unrelated to this competency.

copy.en: The distance around the Earth (its circumference) at the equator is about 40,000 kilometers!
copy.tl: Ang palibot ng Daigdig (circumference) sa ekwador ay mga 40,000 kilometro!
copy.bis: Ang palibot sa Yuta (circumference) sa ekwador maoy mga 40,000 ka kilometro!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Earth's core is the hottest layer!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: create a scale drawing to represent relative thicknesses of the layers of Earth's interior, including the crust, lithosphere, asthenosphere, mantle, outer core, and inner core
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about the core's temperature, but the competency requires creating a scale drawing representing relative thicknesses of Earth's interior layers. The card provides no information about layer thicknesses, scale, or drawing, and does not support the required skill.

copy.en: The Earth's core is the hottest layer! Its center reaches almost 5,000–6,000 °C — that's about as hot as the surface of the sun!
copy.tl: Ang core ang pinakamainit na layer ng Earth! Ang gitna nito ay umaabot ng halos 5,000–6,000 °C — kasing-init ng ibabaw ng araw!
copy.bis: Ang core mao ang pinakainit nga layer sa Earth! Ang tunga niini moabot og halos 5,000–6,000 °C — sama ka init sa ibabaw sa adlaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: One day on Earth lasts exactly 24 hours! That is simply the amount of time it takes for our planet to complete one full spin.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate the rotation of the Earth on its axis using a globe to explain day and night
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that a day is 24 hours and that this is the time for one full spin of Earth. This provides background knowledge about Earth's rotation, but it does not demonstrate rotation using a globe or explain day and night as required by the competency. It supports the concept of rotation but not the specific demonstration/explanation skill.

copy.en: One day on Earth lasts exactly 24 hours! That is simply the amount of time it takes for our planet to complete one full spin.
copy.tl: Ang isang araw sa Earth ay tumatagal ng 24 oras! Iyon ang tamang panahon para makumpleto ng ating planeta ang isang buong pag-ikot.
copy.bis: Ang usa ka adlaw sa Earth molungtad ug 24 ka oras! Mao kana nga panahon aron makompleto sa atong planeta ang usa ka tibuok pagtuyok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earth is about 150 million kilometers away from the Sun
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a single distance fact about the Earth-Sun separation. It does not describe the general structure of the solar system, name major celestial objects, or address their main features and composition, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earth is about 150 million kilometers away from the Sun
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the Sun but does not involve guided observation or description of natural objects seen in the sky, nor does it describe the Sun, Moon, planets, or stars as sky objects. It is only topically related to a celestial object.

copy.en: Earth is about 150 million kilometers away from the Sun—that's really far!
copy.tl: Ang Earth ay humigit-kumulang 150 milyong kilometro ang layo mula sa Araw—napakalayo talaga!
copy.bis: Ang Yuta mga 150 ka milyon ka kilometro ang gilay-on gikan sa Adlaw—layo kaayo gyud!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earth is the third planet from the sun and the only known planet with liquid water and life on its surface!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states a single fact about Earth (its position and uniqueness). It does not describe the general structure of the solar system, name major celestial objects, or discuss their features and composition, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
What makes Earth special?

Earth is the third planet from the sun and the only known planet with liquid water and life on its surface!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nagpapatangi sa Earth?

Ang Earth ang ikatlong planeta mula sa araw at ang tanging planetang may likidong tubig at buhay sa ibabaw nito!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang nakapaspesyal sa Earth?

Ang Earth mao ang ikatulong planeta gikan sa adlaw ug mao ra ang nailhang planeta nga adunay likido nga tubig ug kinabuhi!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earth takes about 365.25 days to orbit the Sun!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the leap year as a calendar adjustment for Earth's orbital period. G6-E-8 requires making a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate observable effects of predictable patterns such as seasons, star patterns, and eclipses. The leap year is not one of these effects and the card does not support the model-building or the listed phenomena.

copy.en: Earth takes about 365.25 days to orbit the Sun! To make up for the extra quarter day, we add February 29 every four years, called a leap year or bisestil.
copy.tl: Tumagal ang Earth ng mga 365.25 araw para umorbit sa Araw! Para mapantay ito, nagdadagdag tayo ng Pebrero 29 tuwing ika-apat na taon, na tinatawag nating leap year o bisestil.
copy.bis: Mokabat og mga 365.25 ka adlaw ang Yuta para mo-orbit sa Adlaw! Aron ma-compensate kini, nagdugang kita og Pebrero 29 matag ikaupat ka tuig, nga gitawag og leap year o bisestil.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Old crust sinks during subduction back into the mantle
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how the subduction of an oceanic plate impacts on the plate above it
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions subduction but does not explain how subduction of an oceanic plate impacts the plate above it. It only states that old crust sinks back into the mantle, with no information about effects on the overriding plate.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Old crust sinks during subduction back into the mantle, while new crust is made elsewhere
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the structures, movements and events that occur at each type of plate boundary
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to subduction and new crust formation, which are events at plate boundaries, but it does not describe the structures, movements, or events that occur at each type of plate boundary. It is a general statement about mantle recycling, not a description of boundary types.

copy.en: The mantle is a giant recycling system! Old crust sinks during subduction back into the mantle, while new crust is made elsewhere.
copy.tl: Ang mantle ay isang malaking recycling system! Ang lumang crust na lumulubog sa subduction ay bumabalik sa mantle, habang bagong crust ang nililikha.
copy.bis: Ang mantle dako nga recycling system! Ang daan nga crust nga molunod sa subduction mobalik sa mantle, samtang bag-ong crust ang himuon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A rock is made of minerals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines minerals and states that rocks are made of minerals, but it does not address exploring, collecting, or describing rocks by texture, color, or grain crystal size as required by G5-E-2.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A mineral is a natural solid with one composition
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that the non-living materials that make up the environment are referred to as 'earth materials'
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses minerals and rocks as natural materials, but it does not introduce or use the term 'earth materials' or teach that non-living environmental materials are referred to by that term.

copy.en: A mineral is a natural solid with one composition, like quartz, gold, or rock salt. A rock is made of minerals, making minerals the building blocks of rocks!
copy.tl: Ang mineral natural na solid na may iisang komposisyon, tulad ng kuwarts, ginto, o asin-bato. Ang bato gawa sa mga mineral, kaya ang mineral ang building blocks ng mga bato!
copy.bis: Ang mineral natural nga solid nga adunay usa ka komposisyon, sama sa kuwarts, bulawan, o asin-bato. Ang bato hinimo sa mga mineral, mao nga ang mineral mao ang building blocks sa mga bato!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It spins around once in the exact same time it takes to orbit Earth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make drawings or a simple model to show the motion of the Earth and Moon relative to the Sun to explain the phases of the moon that people see from Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains synchronous rotation (why we always see the same face), not the phases of the moon, and does not involve drawings or a model as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: We always see the exact same face of the Moon!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to explore and record how and when the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars can be seen moving across the sky
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a fixed appearance of the Moon, not how and when the Sun, Moon, planets, and stars move across the sky, nor any guided activity to explore and record such motion.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It spins around once in the exact same time it takes to orbit Earth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the Moon's rotation and orbit but does not describe the general structure of the solar system, name major celestial objects, or discuss their features and composition.

copy.en: We always see the exact same face of the Moon! It spins around once in the exact same time it takes to orbit Earth, keeping that same side facing us.
copy.tl: Lagi nating nakikita ang parehong mukha ng Buwan! Umiikot ito sa sarili niya sa eksaktong oras na kailangan para umikot sa Mundo, kaya laging nakaharap sa atin ang iisang panig.
copy.bis: Kanunay natong makita ang parehong nawong sa Bulan! Motuyok kini sa kaugalingon sa eksaktong oras nga gikinahanglan aron molibot sa Yuta, mao nga kanunay nag-atubang kanato ang samang kilid.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: That's Earth! Our home is the only planet known to have life in the whole Solar System.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that Earth is the only known planet with life. It does not describe the general structure of the solar system, name major celestial objects, or discuss their features or composition, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Which planet is the only one we know that has living things?

That's Earth! Our home is the only planet known to have life in the whole Solar System.
copy.tl:
Aling planeta ang tanging alam nating may mga buhay na nilalang?

Ang Earth! Ang ating tahanan ang tanging planetang alam nating may buhay sa buong Solar System.
copy.bis:
Hain nga planeta ang bugtong nga nahibal-an nato nga adunay mga buhay?

Ang Earth! Ang atong pinuy-anan ang bugtong nga planeta nga nahibal-an nga adunay kinabuhi sa tibuok Solar System.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because of gravity, the Earth makes one full trip around the Sun every single year!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions gravity as the cause of Earth's orbit, but does not identify gravity as a non-contact force or describe its predictable effects on objects/materials on Earth. It is a different context (orbital motion) and provides no direct instructional support for this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because of gravity, the Earth makes one full trip around the Sun every single year!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the effects of gravity to the motion of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes Earth's yearly orbit due to gravity, but does not involve observing or describing the effects of gravity on the motion of an object in a way that matches the competency's focus on objects' motion (e.g., falling, projectile). It is only tangentially related to gravity's effects.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because of gravity, the Earth makes one full trip around the Sun every single year!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that Earth orbits the Sun in one year, which is a predictable pattern, but it does not involve making a Sun-Earth-Moon system model, nor does it explain seasons, star patterns, or eclipses. It only mentions the orbital period, not the required model or the listed observable effects.

copy.en: Because of gravity, the Earth makes one full trip around the Sun every single year!
copy.tl: Dahil sa gravity, umiikot ang Earth sa Sun nang isang buong pagligid bawat isang taon!
copy.bis: Tungod sa gravity, ang Earth kompleto nga molibot sa Sun kada usa ka tuig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earth orbits the Sun at about 30 kilometers per second
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make drawings or a simple model to show the motion of the Earth and Moon relative to the Sun to explain the phases of the moon that people see from Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states Earth's orbital speed. It does not involve the Moon, phases of the moon, or a drawing/model showing Earth-Moon motion relative to the Sun, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earth orbits the Sun at about 30 kilometers per second
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a speed value but does not teach the concept that speed is how far an object moves in a given time. It is an example of speed, not instruction on the definition.

copy.en:
How fast does Earth zoom around the Sun?

Earth orbits the Sun at about 30 kilometers per second — that's super fast!
copy.tl:
Gaano kabilis umiikot ang Mundo sa paligid ng Araw?

Ang Mundo ay umiikot sa Araw sa bilis na humigit-kumulang 30 kilometro kada segundo — napakabilis!
copy.bis:
Unsa katulin ang Kalibotan sa paglibot sa Adlaw?

Ang Kalibotan moliyok sa Adlaw sa tulin nga mga 30 ka kilometro kada segundo — grabing paspas!
